claims.title: Exact policy-vector frontier recursion for deterministic coarsened law observations
claims.scope: finite rational source-law states, deterministic observation partitions, directed nonempty transitions, deterministic zero-error prefix-code actions, finite horizon, and rational switching penalties
assumptions: one actual hidden law-state path obeys the declared transition relation
the observation class is revealed before each code action
the controller uses deterministic policies with perfect recall
all frontier combinations and dominance checks complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the theorem is a robust set-membership game rather than Bayesian filtering
the bounded frontier method is not a polynomial-time scalability guarantee
the result is not evidence for simulation or a parent-resource bound

claims.title: Componentwise policy-vector dominance is safe in the coarsened-observation recursion
claims.scope: achievable future-cost vectors indexed by possible actual hidden law states in one information set
assumptions: one vector is no larger in every actual-state coordinate and strictly smaller in at least one
parent operations consist of nonnegative stage-cost addition, coordinate selection, and maximization over reachable successors
nonclaims: dominance can fail if omitted policy features create rewards or constraints not represented in the cost vector
Pareto pruning does not prevent exponential frontier growth

claims.title: Deterministic observation refinement cannot worsen the minimizing coder
claims.scope: two observation partitions over identical finite law states where every fine cell is contained in one coarse cell
assumptions: the transition model, code actions, switching cost, initial possible set, and horizon are held fixed
the controller may ignore fine information and emulate a coarse policy
nonclaims: the theorem does not price acquiring or communicating the finer observation
more informative observations need not produce a strict improvement

claims.title: No-observation and singleton-observation endpoints equal independent open-loop and full-feedback games
claims.scope: known initial law state, code-independent finite transitions, identical deterministic code universe, finite horizon, and matching switching penalty
assumptions: the one-cell observation supplies no future state distinction
the singleton partition reveals the exact current law state before code choice
the independent endpoint solvers use the same action and transition timing
nonclaims: the endpoint equality does not identify intermediate coarsenings with either endpoint
partial observation cannot be replaced by the fully observed Bellman recursion

claims.title: Scalar rectangular information-set recursion can overstate a path-consistent hidden-state adversary
claims.scope: deterministic partial-observation games where one hidden state path must obey the transition relation
assumptions: a scalar relaxation remaximizes over every state in the next information set rather than conditioning continuation cost on the actual successor
the exact policy-vector recursion preserves one actual hidden path
nonclaims: scalar recursions are not always wrong; they are exact under additional rectangularity or full-observation conditions
the theorem does not quantify the gap for every game

claims.title: Strict K3 observation-refinement chain
claims.scope: complete confusion on three point-mass law states, identity transitions, two periods, initial uncertainty over all states, and partitions {123}, {1}{23}, and {1}{2}{3}
assumptions: complete binary prefix codes have length vectors that are permutations of (1,2,2)
observations arrive before each code choice
nonclaims: the values 4, 3, and 2 are specific to the declared finite instance
a refinement can have zero value in other games

claims.title: K3 hidden-path frontier separates exact value five from scalar relaxation six
claims.scope: complete confusion on three point-mass law states, identity transitions, no observations, three periods, and initial uncertainty over all states
assumptions: the actual hidden state remains fixed under identity transitions
the code schedule may assign the short leaf to a different state each period
nonclaims: the one-bit gap is not universal
the scalar value six belongs to a stronger rectangular adversary rather than one legal hidden path

claims.title: Bounded exact coarsened-observation policy-frontier audit
claims.scope: the partition, endpoint, strict-refinement, hidden-path, switching, directed-transition, and cap instances exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all code candidates, information-set nodes, continuation combinations, frontier entries, and dominance comparisons complete below declared caps
all costs and law probabilities use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded finite agreement is not a scalability theorem
CI success does not turn the internal game into empirical evidence for simulation
